title: Accepted language check characterization
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let $x,w$ be finite bit strings and $s$ a natural number. The paired encoding of $x$ with the paired encoding of $w$ and the binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the language of accepting configuration codes for $N$ if and only if $w$ passes the following check: its length is $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(|x|)+1$; scanning its first $W(N)(2s+1)$ bits yields an accepting validator state and the head/output summary $(	ext{halted},1)$; the binary value of the next $w_P(|x|)$ bits is at most $|x|+1$; and the final bit is $1$. Here $W(N)$ is the encoded width of one cell block and $w_P(n)$ is the bit width used for an input-head position when the input length is $n$.
hypotheses_covered: A nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean input alphabet
